propositions: Grounding finders (G1G2/E4/E6) flag symbols as missing/unverifiable even when a prerequisite ticket will create them, because they only check the origin/main snapshot and ignore ticket dependencies.

The plan-review prose rule stating 'symbols created by depends_on tickets are treated as existing' is unwired; a deterministic+LLM two-layer citation mechanism `<subject> [rebar:<ticket-id>]` is needed to ground symbols across verified prerequisite edges.

Layer 1 (advisory, never-blocking) must parse `[rebar:<id>]` tokens, verify the cited ticket is a direct upstream prerequisite via BOTH `P.depends_on(C)` and reverse-lookup `C.blocks(P)`, and report unverified citations without blocking.

Layer 2 (LLM coverage protocol, non-deterministic) must check whether the cited prerequisite ticket's plan/file_impact actually provides the specific functionality the grounding finding claims is missing, crediting the citation only on affirmative confirmation.
Reverse-lookup failures (missing ticket, store/network error) must be caught and treated as unverified (fail-closed), never propagating exceptions into the advisory lane.
Both edge-unbacked citations and coverage-absent citations must fall through to the normal missing-symbol block (fail-closed semantics).
